skill.name: ethical-hacking-methodology
skill.description: Guides authorized penetration testing from reconnaissance through reporting, including tool examples, exploitation workflow, Kali setup, and report structure.
skill.summary: Authorized penetration testing methodology with offensive tool examples and reporting guidance.
skill.author: zebbern

security_audit.summary: The skill is an offensive penetration testing guide with explicit commands for scanning, exploitation, brute forcing, Metasploit payloads, persistence, privilege escalation, and disk writes. Several Markdown fence detections are false positives for Ruby execution, but the surrounding instructions contain operational techniques that remain high risk. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed SKILL.md content.

remediation.suggestion: Remove Metasploit exploit steps, Meterpreter persistence, SSH key persistence, and cron backdoor instructions. Replace them with defensive validation descriptions.
Remove Hydra and password cracking commands. Describe password policy testing through approved audit controls instead.

remediation.issue: Active scanning and vulnerability enumeration commands
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit lab-only scope and reduce command examples to non-executable descriptions or safe pseudocode.
Remove dd and raw device partition commands, or move them to a manual setup guide with device selection safeguards.
Remove advice to bypass blocked scans through proxies, packet fragmentation, different scanning methods, or alternative exploits.

content.value_statement: Security teams need a repeatable method for authorized assessments. This skill organizes reconnaissance, scanning, exploitation evidence, and reporting into one workflow.
actual_capabilities: Outlines the penetration testing lifecycle from reconnaissance to final reporting.
Lists common OSINT, scanning, web testing, and exploitation tool categories.
Provides report sections for executive summaries, technical findings, evidence, and remediation.
Summarizes Kali Linux installation and persistent live USB setup steps.
Defines legal and professional conduct requirements for authorized testing.
limitations: Requires written authorization and a clearly defined scope before any active testing.
Includes offensive commands that can harm systems if used outside approved environments.
Does not enforce safety controls, tool rate limits, or legal boundaries automatically.
Needs expert review before use in production or client environments.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Authorized Assessment
use_cases.description: Build a phase-based plan, scope checklist, and deliverable list for a permitted security test.

use_cases.title: Teach Penetration Testing Concepts
use_cases.description: Explain common phases, tools, risks, and reporting expectations in a controlled classroom or lab.

use_cases.title: Structure a Findings Report
use_cases.description: Convert assessment notes into executive findings, technical details, risk ratings, and remediation priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Map an Authorized Engagement
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a scoped assessment.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have written authorization for [scope]. Help me outline permitted phases, evidence to collect, and final deliverables.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Reconnaissance Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate preparation for approved discovery work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a passive and active reconnaissance checklist for [authorized target]. Include boundaries, tool categories, and evidence notes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Controlled Validation Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a lab or client-approved validation.

output: Reconnaissance and scanning phases with evidence goals.
Reporting deliverables for executives and technical owners.

output_examples.input: Assessment notes include outdated software, weak passwords, and missing logging.
output_examples.output: A concise findings summary with severity, business impact, affected systems, and prioritized remediation actions.

output_examples.input: Plan a controlled validation for a suspected injection flaw.
output: Use a lab or approved target only.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization and scope before using any technique.
Keep logs, timestamps, and evidence organized for reporting.
Use controlled labs or client-approved windows for active testing.
anti_patterns: Running scans, exploitation, or password attacks against systems outside scope.
Using persistence, backdoors, or cleanup steps without explicit approval.
Treating example commands as safe for production environments.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for general use?
faq.answer: It contains offensive methodology and should only be used for authorized testing or controlled labs.

faq.question: Does the skill run tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is documentation, but an agent may suggest commands if the user requests them.

faq.question: Can beginners use this skill?
faq.answer: Beginners can study the phases, but they need legal, networking, and security knowledge before testing.

faq.question: What deliverables does it support?
faq.answer: It supports reconnaissance notes, vulnerability summaries, exploitation evidence, and final assessment reports.

faq.question: Which tools does it mention?
faq.answer: It mentions Kali Linux, Nmap, Nikto, Gobuster, Metasploit, Hydra, SQLMap, and reporting workflows.

faq.question: Why may this skill need marketplace restrictions?
faq.answer: It includes exploitation, brute-force, persistence, privilege escalation, and disk device commands.
